bib.title: SWE-PolyBench: A multi-language benchmark for repository level evaluation of coding agents

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "SWE-PolyBench: A multi-language benchmark for repository level evaluation of coding agents", Rashid, Bock (equal contribution), Zhuang, Buchholz, Esler, Valentin, Franceschi, Wistuba, Sivaprasad, Kim, Deoras, Zappella, Callot. Affiliation as printed: "AWS AI Labs" for all authors (Buchholz and Esler "Work done while at AWS"). Venue as printed: "Preprint. Under review." arXiv:2504.08703v3, 23 Apr 2025.

COVERAGE: 20 of 20 pages, 67,337 of 67,337 chars, including appendices A.1 to A.5. References (p12-14) skimmed. Figures 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 are charts: only axis labels extracted, so no bar values were read from them.

CLAIMS (setup for all: full PB, 2,110 tasks, 21 repos; three adapted agents on Claude 3.5 Sonnet, plus Aider-PB with five other LLMs; one run each)

- Pass rate is uneven by language, with Python highest.
  number: Aider-PB Sonnet 3.5: Java 15.8, JS 12.6, TS 13.0, Python 24.1, overall 14.1
  quote: "Sonnet 3.5 15.8±2.86 12.6±1.04 13.0±1.24 24.1±3.05 14.1±0.77" (Table 3, p9). Agentless-PB overall "7.8±0.59", SWE-Agent-PB "10.2±0.66".
- Intervals are bootstrap standard errors over instances, not repeated runs.
  quote: "we report the mean pass rate with associated standard error ( %±SE), estimated via bootstrap resampling over n = 2000iterations" (p9). Footnote 3, p8: "For simplicity, we take here the agent to be deterministic. In practice, agents are typically stochastic."
- Pass rate falls with files to modify.
  number: Aider-PB Sonnet: 17.7 (1 file, n=1085), 13.9 (2), 8.0 (3), 6.9 (4), 7.9 (5+, n=278)
  quote: "Sonnet 3.5 17.7±1.18 13.9±1.72 8.0±1.89 6.9±2.27 7.9±1.63" (Table 5, p11)
- By CST change type, Mixed (class and function) is hardest; class-only is highest but on tiny n.
  number: Aider-PB Sonnet: None 19.8 (n=263), Single Func. 17.0 (848), Func. Only 13.8 (1431), Single Class 40.0 (25), Class Only 36.7 (30), Mixed 9.3 (386)
  quote: "Sonnet 3.5 19.8±2.48 17.0±1.29 13.8±0.94 40.0±9.78 36.7±8.93 9.3±1.48" (Table 8, p18)
- Complexity alone does not explain language gaps: Java is structurally hardest yet beats TS.
  quote: "Java exhibits the highest structural complexity (66.06 % mixed changes, 9.81 average node modifications) yet outperforms TypeScript" (p9)
- By task type (LLM-labelled; 1572 bug, 463 feature, 62 refactor), no consistent ordering across agents.
  quote: Table 4, p10: Agentless-PB "8.8±0.71 5.2±1.03 3.2±2.27"; SWE-Agent-PB "10.2±0.76 9.5±1.34 16.1±4.70"; Aider-PB Sonnet "13.8±0.89 15.1±1.66 12.9±4.25"
- Token efficiency: Aider-PB had the top pass rate on about a fifth of the input tokens.
  quote: avg input/output tokens "315 461 10 900" (Agentless), "338 828 679" (SWE-agent), "64 521 845" (Aider) (Table 4); "utilizes only 19 % to 20 % of the input tokens per instance" (p9)
- Retrieval does not track pass rate one to one. Agentless-PB has the best Python file retrieval (recall 60.9, precision 77.6) but 20.1% Python pass against 24.1% for the other two; SWE-Agent-PB has precision 44.2 at the same 24.1%.
  quote: "high retrieval metrics are (most of the time) a necessary but not sufficient condition for high pass rates" (p10). Table 6, p11, Python file recall/precision: "60.9 77.6", "59.7 44.2", "58.2 73.8".
- Node retrieval is lower than file retrieval: Aider-PB Sonnet node recall/precision Java 29.2/51.1, JS 30.5/39.9, TS 20.2/26.7, Python 36.7/59.9 (Table 6, row "Sonnet 3.5 29.2 51.1 30.5 39.9 20.2 26.7 36.7 59.9").

HOW THE METRICS ARE COMPUTED (p8-9, A.2 p17)
- File level: ground-truth set = file paths changed in the gold patch, predicted set = paths changed by the agent's diff; set recall and precision.
- Node level: build the CST of each changed file, keep class and function nodes (module as root), and for each changed line span take the deepest overlapping node: "the deepest node is the one among all affected nodes that does not contain another affected node". A function change does not count toward its enclosing class. Sets compared are root-to-leaf paths: "Paths(CST(r∗ ∖ r, r∗)) to be the ground truth set and Paths(CST(r′ ∖ r, r′)) to be the predicted set". Labels identify the location, not content.
- The recall/precision formulas and per-instance versus pooled averaging are not written out.

LIMITS
- Conceded: no human check that tasks are solvable; task type and informativeness labels are LLM-made; possible training-data leakage; metrics ignore style, maintainability and security; the multi-file drop may reflect test specificity ("without human annotation of test quality, we cannot definitively attribute this drop solely to task complexity", p10).
- Not shown: no repeated runs, so no run-to-run variance; no pass@k. Retrieval metrics have no intervals. No correlation between retrieval and pass rate is computed; the "necessary but not sufficient" claim rests on reading Table 6 beside Table 3. Retrieval is scored against the gold patch, so a valid fix elsewhere scores low (my inference; the paper does not discuss it). Agents were modified (regression-test validation removed from Aider and Agentless; 18 SWE-agent instances scored as empty), so the numbers are not the upstream agents'. Language is confounded with repository (4 to 6 repos per language). Class-only cells have n=25 to 30. Dated: 2024-era models.

BUILDS ON: SWE-bench [Jimenez et al., 2024] for the F2P/P2P pass criterion; SWE-bench Verified [Chowdhury et al., 2024]; Agentless [Xia et al., 2024] for the issue-informativeness categories; Aider [Gauthier, 2024]; SWE-agent [Yang et al., 2024a]. Tree-sitter is used for parsing.

CODE: none worth keeping (appendix holds classification prompts only).

FIGURES: Figure 1, p2. Two radar charts of pass rate by language and by CST change category for the three Sonnet agents. It shows the language and complexity spread in one image; values must be taken from Tables 3 and 8.

PROBLEMS
- The appendix contains LLM classification prompts ("Your job is to do the following three things..."). These are the paper's data and were not followed.
- Internal inconsistencies: abstract says JavaScript 1017, Table 9 says 1078 final samples; 1572+463+62 = 2097, not 2110 (Table 1 lists 0.61% Misc.). Model printed as "claude-3-sonnet-20241022". Prose says class-only pass rates are "25 % to 40 %", but Table 8 shows SWE-Agent-PB at 52.0 and 46.7. Prose says function changes are "around 15 %"; the table shows 8.7 to 17.0. Page 8 has the typo "fail-to-pass tests ( P2P)".
- Table 1's PB500 per-language file averages (JS 3.6, All 3.2) look odd against the PB row; unverified.
